The team overcame the challenge by performing a value-engineering exercise at the end of the BP1 phase, as well as ION Clean Energy 13 DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT through additional funding by the DOE, ION, and other partners to cover additional costs outside of the project’s control. ION Clean Energy 14 DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT 6 Budget Period 2 – Technical Overview The team commenced BP2 with detailed engineering of the modules and the BOP equipment as well as execution of long lead procurement items needed for the fabrication and installation. BP2 included a 90% 3D model review (Figure 6-1) which included all lines as well as solvent drain and maintenance procedures for operations. Both KMPS and S&L procured long-lead items ahead of final engineering drawings to store either at a Calpine facility or at KMPS’s fabrication shop to further solidify cost and schedule expectations. Engineering drawings were issued to meet California requirements for permanent structures which went through detailed reviews by the California Building Officer (CBO) for approval in parallel with the Air Permitting Authority to Construct process through the Bay Area Air Quality Management District. Construction permits were released in 2022, and the on-site work began shortly thereafter. In parallel with the final fabrication, shipping and installation of the modules, the pilot control software was developed and made ready for factory acceptance testing. Transportation of the CO 2 capture system to the host site (LMEC), the fabrication of the necessary BOP tie-ins, and SAT to verify operations. Figure 6-1: Final 3D Model Issued for Model Fabrication ION Clean Energy 15 DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT The largest challenge of BP2 was the transport and placement of the modules onto the LMEC site. Significant California flooding as well as long-term road closures led to a multi-month transportation period, which impacted scheduling for on-site construction activities. In addition, the lift plan (Figure 6-2) for the modules involved two specialty cranes that had a narrow window of availability. In the future, module routes and shipping companies should be confirmed at the earliest point possible in the project. Concessions in module design such as narrowing the modules, reducing module weight, and/or shortening the modules may benefit the overall project when considering shipping costs early.
